## The question
The user proposes TWO latent spaces aligned by flow matching: space 1 = LF encoder + marker-matrix encoder (an MLP that encodes the
cell's row of the cells x markers matrix, missing entries masked); space 2 = LF encoder + Giemsa encoder (DinoBloom-B); then align
space 2 -> space 1 (flow matching or similar) and decode markers from space 1. The alternative (Claude) is ONE LF-anchored hub: the GS
encoder regresses the LF latent of the same cell (latent distillation, + optional SigLIP), markers decoded by one head on the hub.
The user also wants to test "hidden information": a cell labelled only for CD19 whose embedding lies near CD45-bright cells should be
decodable as CD19+ AND CD45+ -- i.e. marker completion from the shared space, and whether conditioning on the observed marker values
(marker-matrix encoder input) adds information beyond the LF image.

## Build (one package of scripts in your folder; GPU-ready, preempt-safe = resume from <out>/ckpt.pt, save on SIGTERM/USR1)
Fixed for ALL arms: LF features = frozen per-cell features from runs/n029_r18_v4c_fov/probe/lf_feats_all.npy (512-d) concatenated with
runs/n029_r18_v6c_fov/probe/lf_feats_all.npy (512-d) (find the Giemsa cells' own LF rows via lf_feats_hist*.npy / hist_row as
train_gs_bind.py does); labels = targets_tt6c.npz (13 targets: 8 single markers, 4 pooled groups, autofl; mask = observed);
GS encoder = DinoBloom-B image-level exactly as train_gs_bind.py (same aug, freeze 8, bs 128, lr 1e-4, same step count 2500);
cross-slide protocol: --holdout batch1 (train on GS slide of draw 1, test on the draw-2 GS slide) and batch0 (reverse); LF-side models
are trained on non-Giemsa LF cells of FOV split 0 (both draws, as the teachers), validated on split 1, never on Giemsa cells.

Arms:
- A1 two-space + PAIRED bridge flow (user's design, strong version). Space 1: P1 (MLP on LF feats) and E_M (marker-matrix MLP: input
  [y*mask, mask] for the 13 targets, 2x512 hidden, d=256) trained with SigLIP(P1(f), E_M(row)) on labelled LF cells (negatives with
  near-identical observed readouts ignored, as train_bind.py) + decoder D_M: space-1 vector -> 13 targets (masked MSE on both P1(f) and
  E_M(row) inputs, the latter with the decoded entry masked out of the input = no identity shortcut). Space 2: P2 (MLP on LF feats) +
  GS encoder, SigLIP on GS<->LF pairs of the training slide. Alignment: conditional flow matching / stochastic-interpolant BRIDGE from
  z2 to z1 trained on LF cells, where every LF cell gives the pair (P2(f), P1(f)) (frozen P1, P2); small MLP velocity net with time
  embedding, sigma_bridge in {0, 0.1}; inference on a Giemsa cell: z_G = E_G(img) -> integrate 32 Euler steps -> z1 -> D_M -> markers.
- A2 two-space + UNPAIRED alignment (user's design, literal version): same spaces; flow between the MARGINALS only (minibatch-OT
  conditional flow matching, source = z2 of LF cells, target = z1 = E_M(row) embeddings of marker rows from DIFFERENT cells; no
  correspondences). Same inference path.
- A3 LF-anchored hub (Claude). One space: P_L (MLP on LF feats) -> z (d=256) with marker head H (masked MSE, 13 targets) on labelled
  LF cells (+ the same E_M SigLIP term so the hub also carries the marker matrix). GS encoder E_G trained on pairs to REGRESS the
  frozen hub latent of its own LF cell (MSE on L2-normalised z + w_sig * SigLIP(E_G, P_L), w_sig in {0, 0.5}). Markers on GS = H(E_G(img)).
- A0 baseline: re-evaluate the existing TT6c checkpoints with YOUR eval code (identical metrics), do not retrain.

- C1 autofl completion on single-marker cells (they have measured autofl): predict autofl from (a) LF only, (b) LF + the observed
  marker entry via the marker-matrix encoder (autofl masked out of the input), fused model = MLP over [P_L(f), E_M(masked row)] trained
  with random input masking (mask each observed entry with p=.5, predict all observed entries). Eval r on held-out FOVs (split 2) AND
  held-out draw (train draw 1 -> test draw 2 and reverse; the fused model trained on one draw only for that test).
- C2 pooled-panel leave-one-group-out: the 37k pooled cells have 4 group labels (+ grp CD123/HLA-DR/CD14 failing QC in draw 2 = masked

# N054 handoff

Implemented all five stages, A1 paired bridge, A2 unpaired OT bridge, A3 normalized latent distillation, A0 checkpoint inference, M1–M6, and completion protocols. No GPU or container execution was attempted. Scientific comparisons and full-slide baseline reevaluation await your GPU runs.

The standalone package includes `n054_trimodal.py`, `n054_clinical.py`, verbatim contrast dictionaries, selection and submission helpers, the requested Slurm template, requirements, and executable smoke harness. `README.md` and `n054_submit.sh` contain the exact dependency-ordered commands. Launch `bash n054_submit.sh` from this directory on the cluster. The graph has 78 jobs, 12 trainable arm/configuration/direction combinations, two existing baseline checkpoints, one completion stage with three fresh fits, and 14 clinical evaluations. Selection freezes before every held-out GS evaluation. Estimated total: 12–30 A100/H100-class GPU-hours including TTA clinical inference; GPU throughput and Slurm requeue remain unmeasured.

## Verified smoke

Final real-data CPU suite: **passed**, 302.85 seconds. `smoke.log` records commands and stage outputs; `smoke_results.json` contains all 14 tiny-subset evaluation summaries and completion metrics. `smoke_artifacts/index.json` indexes the delivered CSV/JSON tables and NPZ predictions/embeddings/masks. Binary smoke checkpoints remain under `/tmp/codex_n054/final_smoke/` and are deliberately excluded from the delivery.

The common LF universe contains 2,000 cells: 680 train, 660 validation, 660 test. The BSCCM GS universe contains 300 cells: each direction uses 50 training, 50 training-slide validation, and 150 opposite-slide test cells. Each fit runs 20 updates. The stand-in is a random depth-2 ViT-tiny at 32 pixels; LF projections, marker encoder, heads, flow, missingness and split logic use the production code. Both sigma settings, both hub SigLIP weights, both holdouts and all five stages executed. Each clinical smoke used 16 PBC and 24 MLL23 images, producing all 25 registered contrasts; new arms exercised eight-view TTA, while baseline clinical smoke used one view.

Checks passed for held-out-target input masks, finite completion predictions, no GS cells in LF training, source-only completion fits in both draw directions, and source/test row separation. A real SIGUSR1 interruption exited 99, saved `ckpt.pt`, and resumed. Its exported GS weights were **bitwise equal** to uninterrupted CPU training. Completed-stage resume also passed. SIGTERM uses the same registered handler; its delivery through Slurm/Apptainer was not exercised here.

`baseline_compatibility.json` compares 150 same-cell predictions per direction with the original saved GPU `test_preds.npz`. The lowest per-target correlation was .999317 (batch1 holdout) and .999831 (batch0 holdout); autofl prediction correlations were .999885 and .999979. Mean absolute differences were .00552 and .00488 target units, consistent with CPU float32 versus the original GPU bfloat16 backbone. These checks validate baseline model/preprocessing compatibility; tiny-subset M1 values are not full-slide estimates.

Shell syntax and Python parsing passed. `submission_check.json` records a mocked Slurm submission verifying all 78 jobs and that selection precedes all 14 held-out evaluations. No actual Slurm jobs were submitted. `smoke_environment.txt` records the installed CPU dependencies.

## Data corrections and implementation choices

- **C1 is unavailable under the stated label rule.** Direct inspection finds zero single-marker cells with observed autofl in `targets_tt6c.npz`. Its autofl mask covers unstained cells, including GS cells, only. The code emits unavailable C1 rows for every protocol instead of treating placeholder zeros as truth or creating new labels. This does not assert that no raw autofluorescence measurement could be reconstructed elsewhere; that would require a new label/calibration task.
- **The supplied target file does not implement K019's pooled QC mask.** It retains 27,074 failed draw-2 pooled CD123/HLA-DR/CD14 labels. New training and scoring explicitly remove these mask entries, without recalibrating values. A0's own original LF teachers retain their historical training masks for compatibility; the common reference teacher and all scoring use the corrected mask. C2 marks both missing test truth and missing source-draw training truth unavailable for this group. `data_census.json` records the verified counts.
- GS optimization uses only source split 0 and reserves source split 1 for selection: 8,007/994 source train/validation cells for batch1 holdout, 4,495/593 for batch0 holdout. Source split 2 is unused in GS training. TT6c originally trained on the whole source slide, so its training sample count differs. New fits still run exactly 2,500 updates and export their validation-best checkpoint. This implements the requested held-out-FOV selection without exposing the opposite slide.
- New GS image-scale calibration uses source split-0 images only; baseline scaling retains its original `H[:500:5]` rule. The augmentation itself is copied from `train_gs_bind.py`, with production DinoBloom-B/freeze-8 settings. Macenko remains disabled.
- The bridge uses a bounded stochastic interpolant with noise amplitude `sigma*t*(1-t)`, analytic path derivative, zero endpoint noise and deterministic 32-step Euler inference. A2 uses exact minibatch Hungarian OT and explicitly forbids accidental same-cell assignments.
- Completion refits LF projection, marker encoder, both heads and normalization separately for FOV, draw0→draw1 and draw1→draw0. The fixed supplied LF image features themselves come from the specified teachers trained across both draws; the held-out-draw completion claim concerns the newly fitted models, not a source-only image encoder.

## Remaining scientific limits

There is still no GS↔surface-marker truth. M2 products require the stated transitive/CIA assumption; geometry and retrieval cannot establish marker fidelity. C3 is descriptive and cannot verify CD19/CD45 coexpression on singly labelled cells. C1 cannot answer whether a measured single-marker entry improves autofl completion with this target file.

No full-size GPU optimization, CUDA augmentation/backward pass, container dependency check, scheduler signal propagation, or full clinical inference was executable in this sandbox. Smoke metrics test integration and must not be used to rank the arms. Clinical results will be conditional on the one fixed LF-teacher feature pair and seed 0; K025's teacher-run variability still limits stronger clinical claims. Hyperparameter selection is explicitly training-slide autofl r, which need not optimize fine-marker or clinical transfer (K011). All predefined configurations are retained for reporting.

# N054 tri-modal experiments

This folder is a standalone delivery. The BSCCM repository and data are read-only inputs. Training and scientific comparisons require your GPU runs; the delivered CPU smoke uses real data and a random, two-block ViT-tiny stand-in.

**Data corrections:** `targets_tt6c.npz` has **zero** single-marker cells with observed autofluorescence, so C1 returns an explicit unavailable result. It also retains 27,074 draw-2 pooled CD123/HLA-DR/CD14 observations that K019 rejects. Every new model and scorer masks those entries, retaining the original target values otherwise. The baseline's original LF teachers are reconstructed with their original masks; the common reference teacher uses the corrected mask. No labels are manufactured.

## Files and execution

- `n054_trimodal.py`: `lf_spaces | gs_encoder | flow | eval | completion`.
- `n054_clinical.py`, `n054_contrasts.py`: frozen inference and the verbatim registered PBC/MLL23 contrasts.
- `n054_select.py`: freezes the hyperparameter choice using training-slide split-1 autofl r only.
- `n054_gpu.sbatch`: one GPU, partition `preempt`, 16 CPUs, container launch, signal handling/requeue.
- `n054_submit.sh`: exact complete command grid and Slurm dependencies.
- `n054_smoke.py`, `smoke.log`, `smoke_results.json`: executable integration check and results.

Python dependencies are in `requirements.txt`; `timm==1.0.31` is required. There are no imports from repository scripts. The clinical entry point loads its two sibling modules explicitly so `python3 -I` works without modifying `sys.path`.

## Exact GPU commands, in dependency order

From this folder on the cluster:

```bash
cd /home/hpc/v181bb/v181bb10/BSCCM/.agent-research/results/N054-tri-modal-latent-user-two-space-design-l/codex
apptainer exec --bind /hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm /hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm/env/bsccm.sif python3 -I -c 'import torch, timm, numpy, scipy, sklearn, PIL; assert timm.__version__ == "1.0.31"; print(torch.__version__, timm.__version__)'
bash n054_submit.sh
```

`n054_submit.sh` is the executable command list; it prints every exact submitted command and job ID. It submits, in this order:

1. A1 / sigma=0 / batch1 `lf_spaces`, which creates the shared fixed ridge at `runs/n054_reference/ridge.npz`.
2. For **each** holdout `batch1`, `batch0` and **each** configuration `A1:0:0 A1:0.1:0 A2:0:0 A2:0.1:0 A3:0:0 A3:0:0.5` (arm:sigma:w_sig): `lf_spaces`, then `gs_encoder`, then `flow`, then `eval --validation-only`. Every other LF job waits for the reference job; every stage waits for its own predecessor. A3 `flow` is a recorded no-op.
3. `n054_select.py --runs <all 12 run directories> --out runs/n054_selection.json`, after all 12 validation jobs. This file is immutable on rerun unless the identical choices are reproduced.
4. `eval` for all 12 configurations and both A0 checkpoints, after selection is frozen. Reporting the full predeclared grid is intentional; use the frozen choices for the primary A1/A2/A3 comparisons.
5. `completion` once, in the A3/w_sig=0/batch1 directory, after that directory's evaluation. Completion independently fits all three LF-only protocols and does not depend on the GS holdout.
6. `clinical` for all 14 configurations, after each internal evaluation, with TTA=1, PBC all, and the original deterministic MLL23 cap of 1,500 per class. No clinical result affects selection.

For example, the exact commands for a single configuration, submitted serially, are:

```bash
R=/hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm/runs
FLAGS=(--arm A1 --holdout batch1 --sigma-bridge 0 --w-sig 0 --out "$R/n054_A1_s0_w0_batch1" --ridge-cache "$R/n054_reference/ridge.npz")
sbatch --wait n054_gpu.sbatch lf_spaces "${FLAGS[@]}"
sbatch --wait n054_gpu.sbatch gs_encoder "${FLAGS[@]}"
sbatch --wait n054_gpu.sbatch flow "${FLAGS[@]}"
sbatch --wait n054_gpu.sbatch eval --validation-only "${FLAGS[@]}"
# In the complete experiment, freeze selection across all candidates here.
sbatch --wait n054_gpu.sbatch eval "${FLAGS[@]}"
sbatch --wait n054_gpu.sbatch clinical --arm A1 --holdout batch1 --run "$R/n054_A1_s0_w0_batch1" --out "$R/n054_A1_s0_w0_batch1/clinical"
```

Use the complete submission script for the comparison; the single-configuration example is useful for a first GPU runtime check. Do not run two writing stages concurrently in one `--out`. Separate output directories are used for every arm/configuration/direction; clinical has its own checkpoint directory.

Outputs are `runs/n054_{arm}_s{sigma}_w{w_sig}_{holdout}` and `runs/n054_A0_{holdout}`. All defaults in the command list are intentional: seed=0, dim=256; GS freeze=8, batch=128, LR=1e-4, 2,500 updates; LF/flow/completion 2,500 updates, batch=256, LR=1e-3; tau=.25; flow Euler=32. The marker encoder has two 512-unit hidden layers and input `[y*mask, mask]`. All latents are L2-normalized and decoder inputs are scaled by sqrt(dim).

**Planning estimate:** approximately **12–30 GPU-hours** for the complete grid including all 14 clinical evaluations on an A100/H100-class device; roughly 0.3–0.9 GPU-hours per GS fit, with I/O/TTA clinical inference contributing much of the remainder. This is an estimate, not a measured GPU benchmark. The scheduler template requests three hours per stage. Start with the first configuration to measure local throughput and storage load. Preemptions add elapsed time. LF and identical GS fits are deliberately independent across output directories; sharing immutable fits could reduce cost later.

## Splits and objectives

Frozen LF inputs are only the two specified 512-dimensional image feature files. The hist feature/index/hist_row triplets explicitly locate the same GS cell's LF row. Feature standardization uses non-GS, labelled split-0 LF rows only. LF-side spaces and flows train on split 0 across both draws, validate on split 1, and report split 2. The ridge uses alpha=10, an unpenalized intercept, and a fixed target-specific seed to select at most 60,000 observed training rows per target. Its cache is checked against the training rows and normalization; all arms share it.

GS training uses only source-slide split 0, model selection uses source-slide split 1, and evaluation uses **every** FOV on the opposite slide. Source-slide split 2 is unused for GS fitting. Full counts (train/validation/test): batch1 holdout 8,007 / 994 / 5,697; batch0 holdout 4,495 / 593 / 10,015. This reserves validation FOVs that the original TT6c training did not reserve. The baseline is evaluated without retraining.

A1/A2 train space 1 with LF↔marker SigLIP plus masked LF regression and exact leave-one-entry-out marker decoding. Near-duplicate surface readouts are excluded as negatives using the N009 criterion, excluding autofl from the duplicate check. A3 uses LF regression plus that same SigLIP term; its GS objective is normalized latent MSE plus w_sig × SigLIP. A1/A2 jointly train P2 and DinoBloom on source GS/LF pairs with SigLIP. Those models and space 1 are frozen before flow training.

A1 flow endpoints are `(P2(f), P1(f))` of the same non-GS training LF cell. A2 uses independent source/marker-row batches and exact minibatch Hungarian OT; same global-cell matches are explicitly forbidden. Its target is `E_M(row)`, not `P1(f)`. The stochastic interpolant is `x_t=(1-t)z2+t*z1+sigma*t*(1-t)*eps` with analytic velocity `z1-z2+sigma*(1-2t)*eps`. This is a bounded-noise bridge with zero endpoint noise; deterministic inference integrates 32 Euler steps and normalizes the endpoint.

The stain/optics pipeline is copied from `train_gs_bind.py` with Macenko disabled, as in TT6c. New arms fit the 99.9th-percentile image scale on training-slide split-0 images only. A0 retains the original `H[:500:5]` scale for compatibility. The smoke-only backbone/resolution changes are explicit in metadata.

## Outputs and interpretation

Each evaluation writes `eval.json`, `eval.csv`, `eval_gs_preds.npz`, `lf_test_preds.npz`, and, for A1/A2, `lf_geometry.npz`. Validation has separate `validation.*` files and only source-slide split-1 GS cells. NPZs include global rows, hist rows where applicable, predictions, masks/truth, target names and embeddings; LF output includes batch IDs.

- M1: directly measured detrended GS autofl r.
- M2: each target's GS agreement with both the common 1,024-D ridge and its own LF path, paired with teacher-truth r on split-2 non-GS cells of the held-out draw. The product is **an assumption-dependent estimate**, not GS marker truth. The analogous autofl product and measured score are both recorded.
- M3: exact-cell cosine retrieval in the native matching space; pessimistic tie ranks and exact chance rates.
- M4: linear CKA, directed kNN overlap, and mutual-kNN graph overlap, k=10. Mutual overlap is twice the common mutual edge count divided by the sum of both graph edge counts. A1/A2 additionally report mapped-GS↔LF-space-1 geometry and LF-space-1↔LF-space-2 geometry.
- M5: LF-path and ridge r for each target, both draws combined and separately. A0's own LF path is its original two ridge teachers, because TT6c's output head was trained on GS latents.
- M6: per-cell PBC/MLL23 predictions, source filenames, embeddings, class means, and all 10 PBC + 15 MLL23 AUROCs. Contrasts and clinical RGB preprocessing follow the existing script; background is kept.

`completion/completion.{csv,json}` contains C1/C2; `coherence.csv` contains C3. Each protocol trains P_L, E_M, both heads and normalization **from scratch inside its own training draw(s)**. The fused model sees random 50% observed-entry masking during training and predicts all observed entries, as requested. Evaluation always masks the tested target. C2 inputs contain only other observed pooled groups. The failed draw-2 group has no test truth, and in the reverse direction it has no source training truth; both cases are explicitly marked unavailable. C3 conditions on the top 5% observed single-marker values and compares every other decoded marker with the same single-marker evaluation population's decoded mean. C3 supplies no validation of unmeasured marker coexpression.

## Resume and CPU smoke

Reissue the same command and output directory. `<out>/ckpt.pt` contains stage/job cursors, current and best model, optimizer, scheduler, Python/NumPy/Torch/CUDA RNG states. Periodic saves occur at validation boundaries; SIGTERM/USR1 triggers an atomic save at the next optimizer boundary and exit 99. The Slurm wrapper requeues that exit. Evaluation saves GS inference cursors in the same checkpoint; clinical inference checkpoints each batch in its separate output. Feature loading/closed-form ridge computation can be recomputed after interruption. Completed training stages export their validation-best model. Changed training configurations are rejected on resume. Never alter the input files in place between stages.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# preempt-run.sh [--max N] -- <command...>     run INSIDE an sbatch script (templates/preempt.sbatch)
# Lets a checkpointing job live on the preempt / preempt_cpu partitions. Helma facts (scontrol, 2026-10-24):
# PreemptMode=CANCEL (a preempted job is killed, NEVER requeued), GraceTime=900 s from SIGTERM to SIGKILL,
# PreemptExemptTime=2 h (not preempted in its first 2 h), MaxNodes=1, MaxTime=2 days, DefaultTime=10 min.
# On SIGTERM (preemption, scancel) or SIGUSR1 (`#SBATCH --signal=B:USR1@900` = 15 min before the wall time):
#   1. resubmits the batch script saved at the chain's first start, held until this job ends (afterany),
#      with this job's environment + PREEMPT_ROOT/PREEMPT_RESUBMITS (sbatch command-line options and
#      positional args are NOT replayed: put every option in #SBATCH lines, parameters in env vars);
#   2. passes ONE SIGTERM to the command (Slurm signals only this batch shell, measured 2026-10-30); it must checkpoint + exit;
#   3. waits for it. The successor must resume from the latest checkpoint by itself (e.g. --resume auto).
# The command exiting on its own = no resubmit; after a signal, rc other than 0/143 cancels the successor.
# A successor of a run that had already finished must exit at once (resume sees training complete).
# Chain records, ~/.claude/state/preempt-chain/: <job>.info, <job>.next (successor; wait-job.sh follows it),
# <root>.sbatch (the replayed script), stop-<root> (no more resubmits; written by preempt-cancel.sh).
# A plain `scancel` also sends SIGTERM and WOULD resubmit -- cancel a chain with bin/preempt-cancel.sh.
set -uo pipefail
MAX=${PREEMPT_MAX:-20}
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in --max) MAX="$2"; shift 2;; --) shift; break;; *) break;; esac; done
[ $# -ge 1 ] || { echo "usage: preempt-run.sh [--max N] -- <command...>" >&2; exit 64; }
if [ -z "${SLURM_JOB_ID:-}" ]; then echo "preempt-run.sh: not in a SLURM job, running plainly" >&2; exec "$@"; fi
C="$HOME/.claude/state/preempt-chain"; mkdir -p "$C"
find "$C" -type f -mtime +30 -delete 2>/dev/null   # housekeeping: chains older than a month
J=$SLURM_JOB_ID; ROOT=${PREEMPT_ROOT:-$J}; PR_LINK=${PREEMPT_RESUBMITS:-0}  # not "N": an exported job parameter N would be overwritten for the child (Cress 2026-11-09: cascades ran with N=0)
log(){ echo "[preempt-run $(date +%H:%M:%S) job $J] $*"; }
[ -s "$C/$ROOT.sbatch" ] || scontrol write batch_script "$J" "$C/$ROOT.sbatch" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || log "WARNING: could not save the batch script - resubmission will fail"
printf 'root=%s link=%s node=%s start=%s\n' "$ROOT" "$PR_LINK" "$(hostname)" "$(date +%FT%T)" > "$C/$J.info"
log "link $PR_LINK of chain $ROOT (max $MAX resubmits)"

[ -e "$C/stop-$ROOT" ] && { log "stop-$ROOT present: chain stopped, not running"; exit 0; }
child=""; sig=""; resub=0; busy=0
resubmit(){
  [ "$resub" -eq 1 ] || [ "$busy" -eq 1 ] && return; busy=1   # once per job; a failed submit is retried on the next signal
  if [ -e "$C/stop-$ROOT" ]; then log "$1: stop-$ROOT present, not resubmitting"; return; fi
  if [ "$PR_LINK" -ge "$MAX" ]; then log "$1: $MAX resubmits reached, not resubmitting"; return; fi
  local unset=() v out err
  for v in $(compgen -e | grep -E '^(SLURM|SBATCH)_'); do unset+=(-u "$v"); done   # no job env leaking into sbatch

        sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterany:"$J" --export=ALL "$C/$ROOT.sbatch" 2>"$err")

Record the user's tri-modal research plan (2026-11-18), Claude's assessment, and the user's ruling: test BOTH designs, and test the
encoders ("defo do the encoders, it is not a lot and maybe worth it").

entries masked) + a new LF image encoder (fine-tuned/retrained DINOv3 or another encoder: DinoBloom/SuperBloom, ResNet, Cytoland,
live-cell-dynamics models; LED channel selection/weighting); (2) second space LF + Giemsa (same structure, DinoBloom for Giemsa);
(3) align the two spaces with flow matching (alternatives listed: SigLIP, student-teacher, pixel-level OT, SOTAlign, diffusion;
Giemsa<->markers via steering, GNN, discrete flow matching, unbalanced OT, Brownian bridge); (4) maybe decode markers from the
matched space. RQs: RQ1 predict markers from Giemsa; RQ2 align three modalities; RQ3 identify cell distributions in smears.
Geometry checks: CKA, mutual kNN, spectral gap; positive/negative AUROC proxy.

User's "hidden information" idea (2026-11-18): a cell labelled only for CD19 whose embedding sits near CD45-bright cells should be
decodable as CD19+ AND CD45+ -> marker completion through the shared space; the marker-matrix encoder may add information beyond the
LF image when observed marker values are fed in.

## Plan
Claude's assessment (given to the user before the ruling; evidence in brackets):
1. With ONE shared LF encoder the two spaces are already aligned through the LF image (GS<->LF and LF<->MK are both same-cell pairs);
   aligning two separately trained spaces WITHOUT pairs meets the identifiability limit of set-level matching across different cells
   (N034-B: |r| <= .15). Prefer binding both modalities to the LF hub (ImageBind-style); the LF bridge also supplies pairs for any
   cross-space flow.
2. The binding loss must be predictive, not only contrastive: SigLIP/SOTAlign spaces find the same cell (~20x chance) but carry little
   marker information (N009, N045: autofl .38/.18 and .44/.21 vs distillation .72/.60; PBC lineage AUROC ~.55 vs .95-1.00).
   Latent distillation (GS encoder regresses the LF latent of its own cell) is the latent form of the current best bridge.
3. Marker-matrix encoder: most cells carry one scalar (+ autofl; 9 % pooled cells with 4 groups), so a marker embedding is thin; most
   useful as decoder target / for masking and RQ3. Our predictor already decodes all 11-13 markers for every cell from the LF image
   (image-mediated completion); the new part of the user's idea is CONDITIONAL completion (LF + observed markers), testable with truth
   on single-marker cells (autofl measured) and pooled cells (4 groups).
4. Encoders: expected gains modest (N042 low-pass costs <= .011; N050 ConvNeXt errors correlate .94-.96 with ResNet; labels limit),
   but cheap -> test (DINOv3 needs a 24-channel adapter; learned LED gate answers "which LEDs matter", cf. N018 information map).
5. Flow/unbalanced OT fits where no pairs exist: clinical smears (PBC, MLL23) and population proportions (RQ3).
6. Metrics: GOAL v10 (LF->MK, best .6804, target .70); Giemsa: same-cell autofl truth, student-vs-teacher r x teacher-truth r,
   clinical contrasts (PBC, MLL23); geometry diagnostics; AUROC needs per-marker positive definitions (N049: positives ill-defined).
